title: Developer Init Pack: Polyglot Runtime Examples & Ergonomic Patterns
creator: Samir Gupta
description: Create a small, opinionated "developer init pack" of runnable SDK examples and ergonomic patterns for Python (FastAPI), TypeScript (Next.js + Vercel/Serverless), Go (HTTP server), and a cross-platform CLI. Focus on: 1) clear, copy-paste examples that demonstrate retries, streaming token consumption, and structured output parsing; 2) minimal Docker/Vercel/Fly deploy manifests and local dev instructions; 3) cookbook snippets for common production patterns (prefix caching, batch hints, graceful fallback to smaller models). The goal is a low-friction starting point for engineers to build production features with Redwood SDKs and to establish recommended defaults for retries/batching/streaming ergonomics.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Four runnable examples included in repo under /examples: nextjs-edge-chat, fastapi-async-stream, go-http-llm, cli-toolkit.
2) Each example shows: init pattern, retry/backoff policy, streaming consumer example, and structured output parsing with model schema.
3) README for each example with deploy steps for Vercel/Docker and recommended runtime config.
4) CI smoke tests that run the CLI example and basic FastAPI streaming handler (mocked) on PRs.
5) Docs page (Confluence) linking to artifacts and an internal SDK recommendation one-pager.
6) Hand-off notes for Developer Advocacy + Samples team for inclusion in starter templates.
implementation_notes:
Decisions:
- Use SDK idioms: Python async generator for streaming, TS async iterator + fetch streaming APIs for Next.js edge functions, Go channel-based token emitter for server example, and a small CLI wrapper that supports both sync and stream modes.
- Retry strategy: default exponential backoff with jitter, idempotency key for request-level retries for non-streaming endpoints, and per-chunk resume token for interruptible streams.
- Streaming ergonomics: provide a minimal helper wrapper that converts SDK streaming callbacks to async iterators in each language.
- Quantization/Model fallbacks: example demonstrates automatic model fallback policy (large->small) when latency SLOs breached, but actual routing remains a config flag in examples.
Trade-offs: keep examples small and explicit (no heavy abstractions) to be digestible; advanced operator-level features stay in separate Advanced Cookbook doc.
Runtime deps: Next.js 14, FastAPI 0.95+, Go 1.21+, Python 3.11+, Node 20+.
PR checklist: unit tests, smoke CI, example README, sample env files, Dockerfile and a small Vercel config.
